The `VcfVsanDp` PowerShell module under `src/VcfVsanDp/` is a stub that throws on import. Implement it.

The module provides bindings for the VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 vSAN Data Protection (snapservice) API exposed by the Snapshot Appliance. The `VMware.Sdk.Vcf` PowerCLI family ships no binding for this API, which is why the module exists. Those SDK modules are already installed in this environment; declare the dependency in the module manifest rather than vendoring any part of the SDK into the repository.

`docs/contract.json` is the wire contract for the four operations you need, derived from the published OpenAPI specification; `docs/official_sources.json` records its provenance. Read the `serializationRules` block before writing any request code.

Export four cmdlets:

- `Connect-VcfVsanDpServer -Server -Port -Protocol -Credential [-SkipCertificateCheck]` — performs `Snapservice.Sessions_create` and returns a session object whose `SessionId` holds the minted token.
- `Disconnect-VcfVsanDpServer -Session` — performs `Snapservice.Sessions_delete`.
- `Get-VcfVsanDpProtectionGroup -Session -Cluster [-ProtectionGroupId] [-Name] [-State] [-Vm] [-ClusterPair]` — performs `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups_list`, emitting `ProtectionGroupId` and `ProtectionGroupName` per group. Each filter accepts an array and maps, respectively, to the contract's `pgs`, `names`, `states`, `vms`, or `cluster_pairs` query parameter.
- `Get-VcfVsanDpProtectionGroupSnapshotReport -Session -Cluster -PageSize [-StartTime] [-EndTime] [-ProtectionGroupId]` — performs `Snapservice.Reports.Clusters.ProtectionGroups.Snapshots_list`, emitting `ProtectionGroupId`, `SnapshotId`, `SnapshotName`, `Status`, `SnapshotType`, `CreationTime`, `ExpirationTime` and `Deleted` per record.

`tests/drive.ps1` is the authoritative definition of how these are invoked.

Requirements:

1. The snapshot report operation is paginated by offset. Return the complete collection: walk pages until every matching record has been retrieved, and do not request a page beyond the end of the result set.
2. Emit report records in a stable order — creation time ascending, ties broken by protection group id and then snapshot id — so that repeated runs over unchanged data produce the same sequence. The service does not order records that share a creation time.
3. Authenticate `Snapservice.Sessions_create` with HTTP Basic credentials presented up front, then carry the returned token on every subsequent call and stop sending the Basic credentials.
4. Serialize every array filter as one repeated query key per supplied value, preserving the caller's value order. Send optional parameters only when the caller actually supplied them. A parameter that was not set must be absent from the query string entirely, not present with an empty value.
5. Timestamps are contract data. Emit them exactly as the appliance returned them, without reformatting.

Verify with `python3 tests/verify.py` from the repository root. It starts a loopback mock of the appliance, drives your module against it, and checks both the objects you emit and the exact wire shape of every request you make. `docs/`, `mock/` and `tests/` are fixed — make the module satisfy them.

verification.notes: Deterministic and fully offline. The verifier starts mock/snapservice_mock.py on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port, runs tests/drive.ps1 against it, and asserts the emitted records plus the request log in mock/requests.jsonl. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

requirements: Module manifest declares VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager in RequiredModules and no SDK binary is vendored into the repository.
Snapservice.Sessions_create is a POST with preemptive HTTP Basic credentials, no query string and no body.
Every later call carries the minted token in the vmware-api-session-id header and no Authorization header.
Snapservice.Sessions_delete is called at the end of the run.
An unfiltered Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups_list request carries a completely empty query string.
The form/explode=true object parameters filter and iterate are serialized as their properties (start_time, end_time, page_size, offset); the names 'filter' and 'iterate' never appear on the wire.
Every supplied array filter is serialized as one repeated query key per value: pgs, names, states, vms, and cluster_pairs.
Optional parameters that were not set are omitted rather than sent with empty values.
47 records at page size 10 are retrieved in exactly 5 requests at offsets 0,10,20,30,40, with no extra page.
11 filtered records at page size 5 are retrieved in exactly 3 requests at offsets 0,5,10.
Report records are emitted ordered by creation_time, then protection group id, then snapshot id.
Timestamps are emitted verbatim as returned by the API.
